samples.summary: Overlay guard matches Radix *tooltips*, so merely hovering/focusing a header or sidebar button silently kills Esc and arrow navigation in the image viewer
samples.evidence: `OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR` includes `"[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]"`, and `hasOpenOverlay()` (line 32-34) queries the whole document; `onKey` returns early on any match (line 150). Radix Tooltip content is portalled inside a popper content wrapper (`components/ui/tooltip.tsx:38-50`), and the app mounts `TooltipProvider delayDuration={0}` (`App.tsx:74`), so a tooltip mounts instantly on hover *or focus*. On the `/f/:id` image route the Share button is wrapped in `Tooltip`/`TooltipTrigger` (`components/share-dialog.tsx:156-170`) and every `SidebarMenuButton` is a tooltip trigger (`components/ui/sidebar.tsx:535-543`) — the latter renders its content with `hidden={state !== "collapsed" || isMobile}`, i.e. the popper wrapper exists in the DOM even though the user sees nothing. Result: with the pointer resting over the Share button or any sidebar item (or right after closing the Share dialog, when focus returns to its trigger and reopens the tooltip), ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and Escape do nothing at all, with no visible reason. Tooltips are not dismissable layers that own arrow keys, so they should be excluded from the guard (e.g. match `[role="dialog"|"menu"|"listbox"][data-state=open]` only, or exclude `[data-slot=tooltip-content]`).

samples.summary: Guard is a global document query with no relation to the event target, so an overlay anywhere in the tree (or one already animating/hidden) suppresses viewer keys
samples.evidence: `hasOpenOverlay()` does `document.querySelector(...)` over the entire document rather than checking whether the keystroke's target is inside a layer above the viewer (e.g. `t?.closest(OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR)` plus a check that the layer is actually the top-most dismissable layer). Any portalled popper mounted by an unrelated part of the tree — including a `hidden` tooltip content — makes the viewer inert. The converse is also unhandled: a non-Radix modal (no `data-state`) would not match at all and Esc would both close it and navigate away.

samples.summary: Not-found redirect can fire before the workspaces query settles, sending the user to "/documents" instead of the workspace list — and the new file-shell test that asserts "/w/first" is order-dependent
samples.evidence: `documentsPath` comes from `useDocumentsPath(documentData?.workspaceId)` (line 62), which returns `"/documents"` until the `["workspaces"]` query resolves (`use-documents-path.ts:19-21`). The effect at lines 64-69 navigates with `replace: true` the moment `isDocumentError` flips; the document request (a fast 404) can settle before `fetchWorkspaces`, in which case the user lands on `/documents` and the component unmounts, so the later `documentsPath` update never re-navigates. The delta's new test `__tests__/file-shell.test.tsx` ("redirects a missing document to a workspace list") asserts `/w/first` and therefore depends on both mocked promises being flushed in the same batch — a real-world/CI ordering flake as well as a behavioural gap. Gate the redirect on the workspaces query having settled.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR (image-viewer.tsx:22-30) matches "[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]" — the comment even names tooltips — and hasOpenOverlay() (32-34) queries the whole document, with onKey returning early at line 150 before the ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Escape handling (151-153). TooltipContent portals through Radix PopperContent (ui/tooltip.tsx:38-51), so an open tooltip mounts that wrapper; App.tsx:74 supplies TooltipProvider delayDuration={0} for all routes including /f/:id (App.tsx:127). The image route renders FileShell (file-detail.tsx:136-153, file-shell.tsx:108-131) with AppSidebar and the Share button wrapped in Tooltip/TooltipTrigger (share-dialog.tsx:156-170), and SidebarMenuButton tooltips render with hidden={state !== "collapsed" || isMobile} (ui/sidebar.tsx:534-544), i.e. present in the DOM while invisible. Consequently merely hovering (or focus returning to the Share trigger after the dialog closes) silently disables Esc and prev/next navigation. Tooltips never own Esc/arrow keys, so the condition is over-broad — a wrong-condition bug that breaks a core viewer flow. Existing tests only cover a real Dialog (__tests__/image-viewer.test.tsx:91-107), so no guard elsewhere prevents it.

finding.summary: Esc handler is a bare window listener, so closing an overlay (ShareDialog, Select popover) with Esc also navigates the user out of the image viewer
finding.evidence: image-viewer.tsx:113-130 registers `keydown` on `window` and now does `else if (e.key === "Escape" && onClose) onClose()`. The only guard is `t.tagName === INPUT/TEXTAREA || isContentEditable`. The image layout renders `<ShareDialog documentId={documentId} />` (file-detail.tsx:148), a Radix Dialog whose DismissableLayer closes on Escape via a document-level keydown; the event target is the focused DialogContent/SelectContent `div`, not an input, so the viewer's handler also fires. Pressing Esc once to dismiss the share dialog (or a Select dropdown inside it) therefore closes the overlay AND navigates to the documents list, losing the viewer. No `e.defaultPrevented` check, no open-overlay check, and no `stopPropagation` from the dialog prevents this.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that the Esc handler has "no open-overlay check" and its only guard is the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable test — is contradicted by the file. image-viewer.tsx:22-34 defines OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR/hasOpenOverlay() matching exactly the Radix markup the finding cites ([data-radix-popper-content-wrapper], [role="dialog"][data-state="open"], alertdialog/menu/listbox), and image-viewer.tsx:150 executes `if (hasOpenOverlay()) return;` immediately before the ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Escape branches at 151-153. The listener is registered in the capture phase (image-viewer.tsx:155, third arg `true`) specifically so it runs ahead of Radix's document-level dismiss handler, meaning the overlay is still mounted with data-state="open" when the guard evaluates; and since the viewer mounts before any overlay opens, its listener is first regardless of whether Radix binds on document or window. The selector genuinely matches the cited overlays: dialog.tsx:55 renders DialogPrimitive.Content (role="dialog" + data-state) and select.tsx:51-68 renders SelectPrimitive.Content with position="popper" (wrapped in [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]); the ShareDialog at file-detail.tsx:148 is that Radix Dialog (share-dialog.tsx:155,171) with Selects at share-dialog.tsx:182-216. The exact scenario is also asserted by tests at __tests__/image-viewer.test.tsx:91-107, which fire Escape on an open [role="dialog"] and assert onClose/navigate are NOT called, then confirm the same keystroke does close with no overlay. Grep for `function ImageViewer` returns a single definition, so this is not a stale-duplicate confusion. Code is not present as described.
